title: The Star Money (Die Sterntaler)
summary: There was once a little orphan girl whose father and mother had died, leaving her without a home or a single coin. All she possessed in the world was the clothes upon her back and...
full_text:
There was once a little orphan girl whose father and mother had died, leaving her without a home or a single coin. All she possessed in the world was the clothes upon her back and a small piece of bread given to her by a kindly neighbor.

She walked out into the open fields, placing her trust in providence. Along the way, she met a poor starving man who begged for food. The girl handed him her entire piece of bread, saying, "May this nourish you in peace."

Walking on, she met a shivering child who had no cap; the girl took off her own cap and gave it to him. Further along, she met another freezing child with no coat; she gave him her jacket. Finally, in the deep forest as night fell, she met a child with no shirt, and she gave away her own little dress, keeping nothing for herself in the freezing dark.

Standing naked beneath the vast night sky, pure of heart and having surrendered everything to relieve the suffering of others, the heavens opened!

The stars in the night sky began to fall like sparkling rain upon the earth, and as they touched the ground, every star transformed into a hard, glistening gold thaler! At that instant, she found herself clothed in a fine, new linen garment of radiant white. She gathered the star-money in her apron, and lived in joyful charity, sharing her heavenly abundance with the poor for the rest of her days.
moral: Boundless charity that gives its very last possession is rewarded by the riches of heaven.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Star Money (Die Sterntaler)"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
